answer: Reputation is earned through a staged voyage: a new key must serve several epochs of unremarkable, coherent answers before its votes carry any weight, and each stage requires attestation from peers outside its own cluster. A violet flag marks accounts still in probation, so their submissions are visible but cannot gate rewards for others. Forging a marble-solid identity therefore costs not one proof but a long wait with no payoff—while honest agents climb the same ladder at the same speed, and sybils gain nothing by arriving in bulk.
